ov: About 12,000 species of slow-moving arthropods with two pairs of legs on most body segments. Most eat decaying leaves and dead plant matter, and many defend themselves by curling up and releasing chemicals from pores along their sides. Despite the name, only one species has over 1,000 legs.

why.p: Larger millipedes, such as giant African species, are popular pets.

df: Mostly decaying leaves and other dead plant matter; some eat fungi or plant fluids.
fx: Eumillipes persephone, discovered in 2020, can have over 1,300 legs.
The extinct Arthropleura, an early millipede, grew over 2 m long, the largest known land invertebrate.
